intro: A positive activation can receive a negative gradient from the next layer. Trace the chain rule to see why clipping the upstream gradient itself would destroy useful information.
task: Return a dictionary with output = max(x, 0) and dx, the gradient of the downstream scalar loss with respect to x. Use upstream as the supplied gradient with respect to output.
requirements: x and upstream have the same nonempty shape, with at least one axis. Return output and dx as NumPy arrays of that shape.
Pass upstream through wherever x > 0; return zero elsewhere. This lesson explicitly chooses derivative zero at x = 0.
Reject non-finite inputs, scalars, empty arrays, and mismatched shapes with ValueError. Do not broadcast a mismatched gradient.
Do not mutate x or upstream. The sign of upstream is independent of the activation gate.

hints.title: Separate forward and backward
hints.body: The forward pass depends only on x. The backward pass also uses the downstream gradient.

hints.title: Gate, do not clip
hints.body: The local derivative is a mask derived from x > 0, multiplied by upstream.

hints.title: The boundary is a convention
hints.body: ReLU is not differentiable at zero. Follow the stated zero-derivative convention rather than estimating it by a symmetric difference there.

explanation: The chain rule multiplies the local derivative by the upstream derivative. A positive x opens the gate; it does not force the incoming gradient to be positive.
At a negative x, a small change leaves the forward output unchanged, so the local derivative is zero. At a positive x, the local derivative is one.
At exactly zero, the two one-sided slopes disagree. This activity chooses zero for the backward pass. Check finite differences away from that boundary, where a derivative exists.

Change only the sign of an upstream entry attached to a positive activation. The returned gradient should change sign too. Explain what learning signal would be lost by applying ReLU to upstream itself.
